faq.question: Can the truck use the yellow loading curb in front of our Newport Beach office?
faq.answer: Only for a short stop. Newport Beach limits loading at its yellow LOADING ONLY curbs to commercial vehicles and to 20 minutes, far less than a suite takes to load. We use the building's dock, service drive or lot spaces agreed with management instead, and settle that during the walkthrough.

faq.question: What time can a Sunday office move start in Newport Beach?
faq.answer: At 9 a.m. for business addresses in nonresidential zones. The city's zoning code keeps loading there from starting earlier on Sundays and federal holidays, while on weekdays and Saturdays the limit is 7 a.m., before our 8AM start. Whatever the day, our crews wrap up by 6PM.

faq.question: Do you have an office in Newport Beach?
faq.answer: No. SOS Moving works from one office, 5530 Jillson Street, Los Angeles, and dispatches every Newport Beach crew from it. Because this is an Orange County trip, the travel rules on our rate sheet apply: drive time counts double past 10 miles, and a job 30 miles or more from our base has a 4-hour minimum.

faq.question: How much does an office move in Newport Beach cost?
faq.answer: It is billed by the hour: two movers and a truck cost $119 cash or $129 card Monday through Thursday, with higher rates for bigger crews and for Friday to Sunday. Gas adds $30, and each COI your buildings require adds $50. Crew size and the number of phases come out of the walkthrough, and the quote is built on them.

faq.question: Can you move a medical office in Newport Center?
faq.answer: Yes. Exam tables and cabinets, imaging carts and the storage units holding patient records are packed and loaded in a planned order and placed back in the matching rooms at the new suite. We issue the certificate of insurance each building asks for and reserve its freight elevator before the date is fixed.

faq.question: How do you move a large office without closing the business?
faq.answer: We split it into phases, usually one department or one floor per day, spread over several weekends when needed, each finished between 8AM and 6PM. Teams whose phase is not that day keep working, and the project manager keeps the phase list current with you.
